question.text: If two mutual fund schemes invest in the identical portfolio but one charges an expense ratio of 1.5% and the other 0.5%, what will be the approximate impact over a 20-year period on a Rs. 10 lakh investment earning 12% gross return?

answer.text: The lower-cost fund will have approximately Rs. 14.5 lakh more
The difference will be negligible over 20 years
The higher-cost fund will perform better due to active management
Both will have the same final corpus

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM-Series-X-A (p.223) notes that, for an otherwise identical portfolio, lower expenses produce a larger net return, and p.272 uses net return after fees and expenses for comparisons. Net returns are 10.5% and 11.5% respectively. Higher-expense fund: Rs. 10L × (1.105)^20 ≈ Rs. 73.66L. Lower-expense fund: Rs. 10L × (1.115)^20 ≈ Rs. 88.21L. Difference ≈ Rs. 14.54L. The Trap: A 1% annual expense difference looks small in any single year but compounds substantially over 20 years; the net-return gap, not the gross return, drives outcomes. Note: Expense-ratio comparisons should be made on net-of-expense returns over the actual holding period, as the source emphasises returns after fees and expenses.
